findings.issue: The Node `process` global is still open in bot and advice code. It is just as simple as the `global` alias this task closes, and arguably a bigger hole. `process.hrtime()`, `process.hrtime.bigint()` and `process.uptime()` give non-seeded randomness (REQ-028.1). `process.getBuiltinModule('node:crypto')` (available on the repo's Node v22.18) loads a Node module at runtime, which no-restricted-imports and the bot/advice import allow-lists cannot see. `globalThis.process.hrtime()` also passes. D-2's reasoning (no legitimate use in browser-targeted bot code) applies equally to `process`. `process` is a Node global rather than a browser-only one, so BROWSER_ONLY_GLOBALS / no-restricted-globals does not cover it. tsconfig.json includes `types: ["node"]` for src, so these calls also pass typecheck.
findings.evidence: Contributed bot code (the threat model in spec 8) writes `export const r = process.hrtime()[1];` or `process.getBuiltinModule('node:crypto').randomInt(10)` in src/bots/x.ts, src/advice/x.ts or src/engine/bot-random.ts. In-process ESLint with the repo config (lintText, same as the new test) reports 0 errors for each of these: process.hrtime(), process.hrtime.bigint(), process.uptime(), globalThis.process.hrtime(), process.getBuiltinModule(...). In Node (playtest and tests), bot decisions then depend on the clock or the OS CSPRNG instead of the seeded generator. That breaks REQ-028.1 reproducibility, and getBuiltinModule gets around the REQ-025.1 import boundary. grep finds no `process` in non-UI src/, so a ban causes no false positives.
findings.fix: In FUNCTION_AND_GLOBAL_ESCAPES, extend the B6 selector to `Identifier[name=/^(global|process)$/]` + NAME_ONLY_POSITIONS (or add a separate `process` entry with its own probe so it stays load-bearing). Also add `{ object: 'globalThis', property: 'process' }` to botDeterminismConfig no-restricted-properties. Add probes `process.hrtime()` and `globalThis.process` to the new test. If the team decides this is outside the AC, record it as a follow-up task rather than dropping it.

findings.issue: As the spec accepts, the constructor bans do not cover keys built at runtime or a walk over property descriptors. ``f[`constr${''}uctor`]``, `f['constr' + 'uctor']` and `Object.values(Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptors(Object.getPrototypeOf(f)))[4].value` all lint clean in bot code. These are deliberate evasions that code review should catch. This entry only confirms the residual scope listed in spec 'Not doing' and 8. No change is asked for in this task.
findings.evidence: Contributed bot code -> computed key or index into the Function.prototype descriptors -> Function constructor -> arbitrary code (for example, reaching Math.random). Verified with lintText: 0 errors.
findings.fix: None required. Optionally, mention the template-with-expressions form next to the runtime-built-keys note in the B2/B3 comment.

summary: I checked the eight new bans with in-process ESLint and the repo config on src/bots and src/advice probes. They close every named form, plus variants: optional chaining (f?.constructor), unicode-escaped 'constr\u0075ctor', shorthand { global } / { Function }, globalThis?.Function, destructuring { Function } = globalThis, typeof global, and class extends Function. Already covered by existing rules: self/window/frames (no-restricted-globals), indirect eval (no-eval) and string setTimeout (no-implied-eval). The NAME_ONLY_POSITIONS refactor keeps BARE_GLOBAL_REFERENCE's exclusions as they were. The only false positive I found is harmless: a label named `global:`. One equally simple form remains open: the Node `process` global (process.hrtime(), process.getBuiltinModule('node:crypto'), globalThis.process), which lints and typechecks clean in bot, advice and bot-random code (MAJOR). Runtime-built keys and descriptor walks remain open, as the spec accepts (MINOR). No new dependencies, secrets or runtime trust boundaries.
